findings.action: The ADR amendment (and the implementer's notes) claim the measurement records the runtime's CPU time and resident set per scenario, including two simultaneous heavy checks, and a qualifying third run; the committed report (.pose/reports/2026-11-09-pose-worktree-runtime-measurements.md:19-40) and its JSON hold two runs with no CPU figure, no per-scenario memory, no T7 and no two-heavy scenario (report unchanged since 89a65914). The exit gate's RAM/CPU/latency per scenario with simultaneous jobs therefore still has no evidence, and T7 is absent from R8 of pose-worktree-runtime-qos-and-measurement (spec :43 lists T1-T6), so it was not fixed in the spec before the numbers.
Count in Busy only commands whose handler has answered (or subtract the open hosted connections) and test a stop during a normal hosted run.
findings.rationale: busy is incremented at admission (cli/runtime_host.go:124), not only after a deadline as the Busy doc (:259) says, so a running command whose connection is still open counts in both inflight and busy: stop reports drained or abandoned 2 for one command, and status InFlight (:503) is one too high; the new test only covers busy with no open connection.

findings.rationale: Measurement harness gaps: cpuIdleShortEnd is computed and discarded so short_idle has no CPU figure; the clock tick is hard-coded to 100 (:71); the per-scenario memory figure is VmRSS read after the scenario rather than its peak.
